headline: Monero drops 11% as Spain's crypto-freeze law targets privacy coins; Bitcoin's Thanksgiving gains fade
summary: Monero fell 10.68% — its worst single day in over five months — after Spain enacted legislation allowing authorities to freeze privacy-focused cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin briefly reclaimed $61,000 before retreating to $59,950, and a technical 'death cross' pattern is now forming on its chart, a signal that has historically preceded further near-term weakness. The rest of the market was mostly quiet, with Hyperliquid and Zcash the notable exceptions to the downside drift.

winners.name: Bitway
winners.catalyst: No specific catalyst was cited in the researcher's data; the gain appears to be technical movement on light volume.

losers.name: Monero
losers.catalyst: Spain's new crypto-freeze law, which specifically targets privacy coins, continued to drive sustained outflows from XMR — marking the asset's largest single-day decline in more than five months.

whyItMoved:
The day's clearest story was regulatory pressure on privacy coins. Spain passed legislation enabling authorities to freeze crypto assets, with privacy-focused coins like Monero named as a primary target. XMR fell 10.68% — its steepest single-day drop in more than five months — as traders exited the asset following a second consecutive session of regulatory-driven selling. Zcash, another privacy coin, moved in the opposite direction, rising 5.32%. The researcher's data cited no specific catalyst for ZEC's gain; it may reflect traders rotating into a privacy-coin alternative perceived as carrying lower regulatory risk, though that reading is speculative.

Bitcoin's post-Thanksgiving bounce proved short-lived. BTC briefly reclaimed $61,000 before retreating to $59,950, a decline of 0.73% on the day. The more significant development is a 'death cross' now forming on Bitcoin's chart — this occurs when the 50-day moving average crosses below the 200-day moving average, a pattern that has historically preceded further near-term weakness, though it is a lagging indicator and not a reliable standalone signal. Ethereum followed Bitcoin lower, slipping 0.85% to $1,669.28.

Hyperliquid was the day's standout gainer among tracked assets, rising 6.71% to $64.47 with no specific catalyst cited in the researcher's data. Solana gained 1.62% and Dogecoin added 2.05%, both moving against the broader drift. The Fear & Greed index sits at 12 out of 100 — deep in 'Extreme Fear' territory — reflecting the cautious tone across the market.
worthKnowing: Binance restored full withdrawal functionality after a month-long suspension triggered by a $6.4 billion hack — the largest exchange breach in recent memory.

The incoming ECB president signaled a preference for tokenized bank deposits over stablecoins and Bitcoin as Europe's digital money framework, a stance that could shape regulatory headwinds for crypto in the EU.
Ethereum developers scheduled the Glamsterdam upgrade for the Hoodi testnet on December 15, advancing the next major protocol improvement toward mainnet.
